_readme: The cross-repo contract, as data rather than prose.
Six CLIs compose by piping JSON into one another, and until now the only
record of what they emit was AGENTS.md. Prose drifts silently: a renamed
key leaves every test green, and a driving agent that guesses wrong sees
`null` from jq, which reads exactly like an absent answer.
Each repo has a test that loads this file and asserts its own slice, so a
rename now breaks a build instead of a reader. Each tool also prints its
slice with --contract, so an agent can ask rather than be told.
Bump `contract` whenever anything below changes, and update the siblings
and AGENTS.md in the same pass — that is the repos' standing agreement.

exit_codes._note: One table for every tool in the fleet, the account tools included. WHICH exits carry a JSON body on stdout is per tool: read body_on. Every other exit ends stderr with the error line described under error_body.
exit_codes.0: success — the JSON body is on stdout
exit_codes.1: error: a source is down, blocking, or answered something unreadable. Retry later; the entity may still exist
exit_codes.2: usage error: fix the command line
exit_codes.3: nothing, or too many things, matched. The candidates are on stdout, as exit_3_body describes, each carrying the id to re-run with
exit_codes.4: resolved, but nothing to report. A real, final answer — record it and move on
exit_codes.5: setup required: credentials, a session, or a missing browser. Do not retry unchanged

_note: Exit 3 used to differ by tool: bolig printed candidate objects, tinglysning
printed bare label strings, and cvr printed prose on stderr and left stdout
empty. An agent reading the wrong stream saw nothing, which reads exactly
like 'there were no candidates' and ends a search that should have narrowed.
One shape now, on stdout, for every tool whose exit_codes include 3.

error.not_found: nothing matched. `candidates` holds fuzzy did-you-mean guesses and may be empty
error.ambiguous: several matched. `candidates` is the narrowing list

candidate_keys._note: Every candidate is an object: `label`, plus the identifier the SAME tool accepts as input, so picking one needs no second resolution.

_note: Every exit without a stdout body ends STDERR with one line of compact JSON.
It is on stderr on purpose: an error envelope on stdout would answer
`jq '.people | length'` with 0, which is a failure reading as an answer.
Prose and usage text may precede it; it is always the last line.

codes.USAGE: exit 2 — the command line is wrong; `hint` says how
codes.SETUP: exit 5 — credentials, a session or a browser is missing. For the account tools `hint` names the offline commands that still work and says to ask the user before any login
codes.NETWORK: exit 1 — the source could not be reached
codes.UPSTREAM: exit 1 — the source answered with an error, or with a shape this tool cannot read
codes.BLOCKED: exit 1 — bot protection, a rate limit or a waiting room

stdout.json: compact (one line) when stdout is not a TTY, indented at a TTY. Pipe through `jq .` to read it.
stdout.help: `--help` prints to stdout and exits 0, and `<tool> <command> --help` prints that command's own. A usage error exits 2 and ends stderr with the error line, whose `hint` names the --help to read; usage text before it is optional, because a usage dump on every typo is tokens an agent pays for.

join_keys._note: DAWA UUIDs at two granularities. Match on these, never on the printed address, which is lossy. Paths are keyed by command, matching tools.<tool>.commands.

door.meaning: the street door; equal for every home behind it

home.meaning: the individual dwelling; the only join that is exact in a block of flats
home._cvr: cvr emits no home key: the register records a floor but never a door, so a company address cannot name one dwelling.

cvr.accepts_number: wherever a command takes <query>, a CVR number may be bare (24256790), grouped with spaces or dashes (24 25 67 90), or carry its VAT prefix (DK24256790). The exit-3 body still reports the query exactly as typed.
cvr.exit_3_candidates: Every candidate carries both ids and the one that does not apply is null. A company candidate sets `cvr`, which every <query> command takes; a person candidate (only from `person`) sets `unit`, which `cvr person --unit` takes. Companies are listed largest first, people with the most companies first. A rejected name is `not_found` with the register's fuzzy guesses as candidates; only a genuine tie between matching names is `ambiguous`.
cvr.table_output: --format table (the default at a terminal) is for a person and is outside this contract: exits 3 and 4 then say what they have to say as prose on stderr, and stdout may be empty.

notes.optional: every key but cvr, name and source is omitted when the register holds nothing for it, so read them as `.status // empty`. `bankrupt` and `advertising_protected` are present only when true.
notes.access_address_id: DAWA's uuid for the street door — the fleet's join key, which bolig and tinglysning take in place of an address. Absent, with `warnings` saying why, when DAWA could not settle on exactly one door. Door granularity only: the register records a floor but never a door.
notes.people: present only when credentials are configured AND the lookup was by number; a lookup by name never carries it. `ownership` is the floor of a band, not a share: 0.25 means at least 25%.
notes.source: which register answered: cvrapi.dk or apicvr.dk without credentials, cvr-permanent with.

on_exit_4._note: The body is the empty array itself: `.` is the whole body, in the jq grammar the other paths use.

notes.rows: company records as `company` prints them, without `people`, `warnings` and the address join key: run `cvr company <cvr>` on a row for those. Names only are matched — never addresses, people or industries.
notes.limit: --limit caps the rows (default 20, at most 3000); the source reports no total, so a full page may be a truncated one.

on_exit_4._note: The body is the empty array itself: `.` is the whole body, in the jq grammar the other paths use.

notes.order: newest period first. --limit caps the rows (default 200, at most 3000).
notes.documents: `url` needs no credentials. mime_type application/xml, application/xhtml+xml and text/html are machine-readable XBRL, which `facts` and `financials` parse; application/pdf is the rendering a person reads; image/tiff is a scan with nothing to extract.

on_exit_4._note: The company resolved and has published no machine-readable statements. `note` says so.

notes.warnings: caveats on figures that ARE present: a change of currency, basis, framework or period length, or a filing tagged at the wrong scale. Read as `(.warnings // [])`.
notes.fetch_errors: figures that are MISSING: a filing that could not be downloaded or read. A year absent from `periods` beside an entry here was not skipped by the company.
notes.periods: oldest first. Amounts are in `currency`, or per period in `.periods[].currency` when `mixed_currency` is true. `revenue_growth_pct` and `profit_margin_pct` are withheld across a break rather than computed through it; `scale_disputed` marks a period two filings state a power of ten apart.

on_exit_4._note: The body is the empty array itself: `.` is the whole body, in the jq grammar the other paths use.

notes.rows: the `.periods[]` of `financials` without the derived keys — and without `warnings` and `fetch_errors`, which a bare array has nowhere to carry: a filing that failed to download is reported on stderr only. Prefer `financials | jq .periods`.

on_exit_4._note: Either nothing was readable — no filing, no XBRL, or a cover page without accounts, and `note` says which — or --concept matched nothing in the filing that was read.

notes.headline: true when the fact is a total rather than a component of one. A concept is reported once as the total and again for every breakdown and comparative year, so select on `.headline` before reading a figure as THE figure.
notes.dimensions: an object mapping each breakdown axis to the member selected on it; absent on a total. Its keys are the filing's own and are not declared here.
notes.period: a fact carries either period_start and period_end (a duration) or instant (a balance-sheet date), never both.
notes.notes: tagged prose, markup stripped. Without --concept the whole filing comes out, which is large: narrow it.

on_exit_4._note: The body is the empty array itself: `.` is the whole body, in the jq grammar the other paths use.

notes.rows: one row per person per role, so a director who also owns appears twice. Needs credentials (exit 5 without).
notes.ownership: the floor of a band, not a share: the register records ownership in intervals, so 0.25 means at least 25%. Summing or multiplying it understates.

on_exit_4._note: The body is the empty array itself: `.` is the whole body, in the jq grammar the other paths use.

notes.rows: one row per company per role for ONE participant; `company_cvr` feeds any <query> command. A name several participants share exits 3 with a `unit` per candidate, never a merged list. Needs credentials (exit 5 without).
notes.limit: --limit caps the participants matched, not the rows returned.

notes.passthrough: the Elasticsearch 6.8 reply, unmodified and undeclared here: documents under .hits.hits[]._source, and .hits.total a plain integer rather than the {value, relation} object of later versions. Always JSON; --format table is a usage error. Needs credentials (exit 5 without).

bolig.accepts_uuid: a bare DAWA uuid as the positional argument skips resolution entirely: a home's own id (this tool's .address.id, .addressUnitId from tinglysning and dgs), or a street door's (.accessAddressId), which resolves when exactly one home sits behind it and otherwise exits 3 with each home's id as a candidate

on_exit_4._note: No valuation exists for the address (a plot, a new build, a commercial unit). The body has the SAME keys as exit 0, so one reader handles both: `null` lists the keys that are always null here, `nullable` the ones that may be, `empty` the arrays that are always []. `history` and `property` are still looked up and filled in when Boliga has them, and both join keys are present, so the address can go straight to tinglysning.

nested._note: What is inside the top-level keys, keyed by jq path in the grammar join_keys uses: a trailing [] means every element of that array. `keys` are always present, `optional` may be absent, `nullable` may be null. `.warnings` and `.sources` are arrays of strings and have no entry.

notes.warnings: empty array is a real claim: every hop answered. Non-empty means part of the result is missing rather than absent.
notes.history: an empty history beside a history warning is 'not looked up', not 'never traded'. `kind` is "sold" or "listed"; `price` is the sale price or the asking price accordingly, and `saleType` exists only on a sale.
notes.valuation: `value` is the headline: the mean of `included`. `spread` is the low and high of `included` only, and `excluded` is what the model discarded, usually the stale public assessment. `annualTrendPct` is a yearly rate fitted over `trendYears` years.
notes.nearbySales: comparable homes for sale now: asking prices, not sold ones.
notes.address: `floor` and `door` are "" for a house, never null.
notes.property: BBR facts as Boliga holds them. `boligaId` is Boliga's own GUID, not a DAWA id and not a join key. null means no BBR row was read, and `warnings` says which reason.

tinglysning.accepts_uuid: a bare DAWA uuid as the positional argument, wherever an address is accepted. A home's own id (this tool's .addressUnitId, dgs's .addressUnitId, bolig's .address.id) reads that one home's deed: the row is chosen by label EQUALITY, never by position, so --index beside it is exit 2 and a home no row carries is exit 3 with the door's roster as candidates. A street door's id (.accessAddressId) behaves exactly like the door's address typed out, --index included. Only DAWA answering 404 for the id is exit 3; DAWA being down is exit 1

on_exit_4._note: Two different final answers exit 4, and `propertyCount` tells them apart. 0: NO PROPERTY is registered at the door — `units` is [] and everything describing a deed is null (`property`, `propertyType`, `propertyIndex`, `addressUnitId`, `charges`, `chargesTotal`, `publicAssessment`), while `address` and `accessAddressId` are what did resolve, so the door can still go to bolig. 1 or more: the deed WAS read and lists no owners — the body is an ordinary exit-0 result whose `owners` is []. Both have the SAME keys as exit 0, so one reader handles all three. `null` is empty because no key is null in both cases.

nested._note: What is inside the top-level keys, keyed by jq path in the grammar join_keys uses: a trailing [] means every element of that array. `keys` are always present, `optional` may be absent, `nullable` may be null. `.units`, `.warnings` and `.charges[].creditors` are arrays of strings and have no entry.

notes.warnings: everything that makes the result less trustworthy than it looks: the condominium parent record, shares that do not sum to 1, a zero share, an unresolved unit id, charges that were not read, a unit id answered with the whole building's deed. Read it on every result; an empty array is a real claim.
notes.owners: the registered owners (Adkomster), de-duplicated — the register repeats each owner once per deed. `share` is a fraction as text ("1/2"), null when the register shows none. On a block of flats, --index 0 is usually the parent record, whose one `name` is a note like "Opdelt i ejerlejlighed 1-84" and not a person; `warnings` says when.
notes.charges: what is registered AGAINST the property (Hæftelser), beside who owns it. `principal` is what the deed was REGISTERED for, never the balance still outstanding — a deed is not written down in the register as it is repaid. null (not []) means the charges were never read: only the API payload carries them, so `source: "dom"` always has null here. [] means none are registered. `id` is the deed's alias (date-number); `rateType` is "fixed" or "variable"; `principalText` exists only on a charge whose principal could not be parsed, and holds the raw string.
notes.chargesTotal: the principals summed: an UPPER BOUND on debt, not a debt figure. Do not subtract it from a bolig valuation and report the result as equity. null when `charges` is null, or when any principal failed to parse — `warnings` names how many.
notes.publicAssessment: the offentlig ejendomsvurdering the tingbog carries, with the date it was set. The same figure bolig reports under .valuation.excluded as 'Den offentlige ejendomsvurdering' — often years stale, which `assessedAt` makes visible without a second lookup.
notes.units: the label of every property behind the door, in --index order and complete (the stderr listing stops at ten). `units[propertyIndex]` is the row that was read and `propertyCount` is its length. One deed is read per call.
notes.property: the label of the deed that was read. Hand THIS to bolig for a specific flat, never `address`, which is the door — or better, hand it `addressUnitId`.
notes.addressUnitId: null is deliberate, never a guess: the parent record is not a home, and a label that matches no single DAWA unit is withheld. `warnings` says which.
notes.source: "api" is the JSON the page itself received. "dom" is the fallback that scrapes the rendered page: it reads owners only, so `propertyType`, `charges`, `chargesTotal` and `publicAssessment` are null beside it.

never_emits.3: an ambiguous name is answered with a ranked list at exit 0; there is no candidate list to refine from

on_exit_4._note: The directory has nothing to report. Two cases, both positive evidence from the site: it rendered its result list and the list was empty (nobody matches the query), or `page` is past the last page and it answered 404 — then `warnings` says so, because `count` 0 on page 3 is not 'nobody has this name'. Same keys as exit 0, with `count` 0 and `hasMore` false. An unreadable, blocked or unreachable page is never this — it is exit 1, and so is a 404 on page 1.

nested._note: Keyed by jq path in the grammar join_keys uses: a trailing [] means every element of that array. `keys` are always present, `nullable` may be null. `.warnings` is an array of strings and has no entry.

notes.query: the input exactly as typed. A city or postal code narrows a search only when it is part of the query ("fornavn efternavn by"): the site has no separate where-field. A phone number may be spaced or carry +45.
notes.limit: the --limit that was asked for, or null. `people` holds at most that many rows, from the top of the ranking, and only those were resolved through DAWA.
notes.count: the people on this page of the site, NOT the length of `people`: --limit does not change it, so `count > (.people | length)` means the list was cut.
notes.hasMore: about the site's page of 25 rows, counted before deduplication: true means `--page <page + 1>` has more.
notes.people: the site's own ranking. An ambiguous name is answered with this list rather than refused. The profile-only fields (givenName, familyName, coordinates) are not on a row; `dgs person <id>` has them.
notes.warnings: names each withheld join key and why, and says when `page` was past the last one. An empty array is a real claim: every address resolved.

on_exit_4._note: No such profile: the site answered 404 for this id. Same keys as exit 0, with `found` false and everything but `id` and `found` null. A page that loaded without a person on it is never this — it is exit 1.

notes.found: tags the envelope: true at exit 0, false at exit 4. `jq 'select(.found)'` keeps the hits.
notes.id: the id that was asked for, never null.
notes.coordinates: the map pin the site drops on the address, as numbers. null when the profile carries no map link.

aula._note: The account tool: it reads the user's own children's school and daycare, logged in as the user, and sits outside the join graph on purpose — no join key leads into it, and --contract prints no join_keys. Exit 5 is a missing or rejected session, and its error line never says to log in: a login costs the user a MitID approval on their phone, and the hint names what still answers without one and says to ask the user first. Exit 4 is a read that worked and came back empty, body still printed. `doctor` is the one exit 1 that also has a body (its report). --json is accepted and ignored; JSON is the default, one line on a pipe.

bridge.emits: that guardian's `address` — `{ street, postalCode, city }`, or null — when the family chose to share it in Aula. Text, not a DAWA id: it goes to bolig or dgs as a query.
bridge.boundary: aula is only ever called with a name the USER typed. A name discovered by another tool goes to dgs or cvr, never here.

notes.digest: never exits 4 or 1 for one of its parts: a dozen reads in one payload, each degraded on its own. `fetchWarnings` names a calendar or presence read that failed (its array is then []), `calendarAvailable` says whether the calendar read worked, and `weeklyPlans[].status` says which plans are partial or failed.
notes.fetchedAt: when the oldest response in the payload was read from Aula; `generatedAt` is when the payload was assembled. Minutes apart means the answer came from the ten-minute cache.
notes.attention: the signals Aula itself flags, as a starting point and not the answer. `sessionIsSteppedUp: false` under `family` means sensitive threads may be masked or missing.
notes.threads: every message body is included (`messages[]`); `messagesUnavailable` is a thread Aula refused, `messagesIncomplete` a thread that lost a page, `messageReadWarning` says why. `latestMessagePreview` is cut mid-word by Aula itself.
notes.collectionLimits: non-null only when `--limit` cut that list: the limit that did. Null means the window bounded the read.
notes.attachments: an attachment is a position, never a URL: `index` is what `attachment <threadId> <index>` (numbered across the whole thread) and `post-attachment <postId> <index>` (numbered within the post) take; both save the file and print its path. `kind` is file, media or link; `link` is set only for a link, which is an ordinary web address someone pasted. `index` is null when only part of a thread was read (one --page, or messagesIncomplete true): the position cannot be known, so re-read before downloading.
notes.weeklyPlans: `status` is what tells a failed vendor read from a quiet week — both are `items: []`. ok: the vendor answered for every child asked. partial: items are real and `warnings` names who is missing. failed: nothing readable came back and `warnings` says why — never an empty week. skipped: the vendor was not asked, because no selected child attends a school. `provider: "unavailable"` is a capability that threw before any vendor answered. `items[]` keys are whatever the vendor gave: every one is optional, and `date` may be an ISO date or the vendor's own Danish label.

notes.envelope: `truncated: true` means more rows matched than are here — raise --limit, or narrow with --since where the command takes it. `limit` is null when nothing capped the read (`--since` alone, or a command with no default cap). `fetchedAt` is when the oldest response in the answer was read from Aula; responses are cached ten minutes, and --no-cache makes it now.
notes.threads: newest first. `latestMessagePreview` is cut mid-word by Aula itself; the `optional` keys appear with --full, which reads every message (`messages[]` as in `thread`), and `messageReadWarning` is then nullable.
notes.attachments: an attachment is a position, never a URL: `index` is what `attachment <threadId> <index>` (numbered across the whole thread) and `post-attachment <postId> <index>` (numbered within the post) take; both save the file and print its path. `kind` is file, media or link; `link` is set only for a link, which is an ordinary web address someone pasted. `index` is null when only part of a thread was read (one --page, or messagesIncomplete true): the position cannot be known, so re-read before downloading.

notes.messages: every page, in order, unless --page names one — then `messagesIncomplete` is null (one page says nothing about the rest) and every attachment `index` is null.
notes.attachments: an attachment is a position, never a URL: `index` is what `attachment <threadId> <index>` (numbered across the whole thread) and `post-attachment <postId> <index>` (numbered within the post) take; both save the file and print its path. `kind` is file, media or link; `link` is set only for a link, which is an ordinary web address someone pasted. `index` is null when only part of a thread was read (one --page, or messagesIncomplete true): the position cannot be known, so re-read before downloading.

notes.envelope: `truncated: true` means more rows matched than are here — raise --limit, or narrow with --since where the command takes it. `limit` is null when nothing capped the read (`--since` alone, or a command with no default cap). `fetchedAt` is when the oldest response in the answer was read from Aula; responses are cached ten minutes, and --no-cache makes it now.
notes.posts: newest first; `important` is Aula's own flag. `groups` names who a post was shared with.
notes.attachments: an attachment is a position, never a URL: `index` is what `attachment <threadId> <index>` (numbered across the whole thread) and `post-attachment <postId> <index>` (numbered within the post) take; both save the file and print its path. `kind` is file, media or link; `link` is set only for a link, which is an ordinary web address someone pasted. `index` is null when only part of a thread was read (one --page, or messagesIncomplete true): the position cannot be known, so re-read before downloading.

notes.envelope: `truncated: true` means more rows matched than are here — raise --limit, or narrow with --since where the command takes it. `limit` is null when nothing capped the read (`--since` alone, or a command with no default cap). `fetchedAt` is when the oldest response in the answer was read from Aula; responses are cached ten minutes, and --no-cache makes it now.
notes.albums: metadata only, never the photos, and no photo count: Aula's cover preview is capped at one and cannot be counted. `createdAt` is the album's creation day, usually the day of the event but it can lag a day. The synthetic id-less bucket Aula prepends is dropped.

notes.window: forward only: from today, --days ahead, at most 50 — Aula refuses longer windows. `children` names the family's children the event belongs to. `responseRequired` with `responseStatus` other than accepted is an invitation awaiting an answer, and this tool cannot answer it.

notes.status: today only. `status` is the English gloss and `statusDanish` the label Aula's own module shows: Ikke kommet, Syg, Ferie/fri, Kommet/til stede, På tur, Sover, Gået. An institution that does not use komme/gå answers nothing (exit 4).

notes.days: the recurring komme/gå plan a guardian registered, one row per child per day — what is planned, where `presence` is what happened today. `pickupType` is Aula's henteform in English: collected by a named person, may leave alone within a window, leaves alone at the exit time, leaves with a named person.

on_exit_4._note: one row per child, each with `groups: []`

notes.classGroupId: the group `contacts` and `birthdays` read by default; null when Aula does not label a class, and --group <id> then names one.

notes.role: --role child (the default) lists the class; --role guardian lists the parents, and is the fleet's bridge: `address` is the guardian's own, when the family chose to share it, and null otherwise. `birthday` is shared only for children, and its year may be a placeholder. `relations` are a child's guardians or a guardian's children.

notes.envelope: `truncated: true` means more rows matched than are here — raise --limit, or narrow with --since where the command takes it. `limit` is null when nothing capped the read (`--since` alone, or a command with no default cap). `fetchedAt` is when the oldest response in the answer was read from Aula; responses are cached ten minutes, and --no-cache makes it now.
notes.birthdays: classmates whose guardians shared a birthday, soonest first. `date` is MM-DD (Aula shares day and month only); `turns` is null when the year is a placeholder.

notes.type: the badges Aula is showing right now; `type` is Aula's notificationEventType (NewMedia dominates).

notes.attachments: every attachment in the thread, in message order, with who sent it and when. an attachment is a position, never a URL: `index` is what `attachment <threadId> <index>` (numbered across the whole thread) and `post-attachment <postId> <index>` (numbered within the post) take; both save the file and print its path. `kind` is file, media or link; `link` is set only for a link, which is an ordinary web address someone pasted. `index` is null when only part of a thread was read (one --page, or messagesIncomplete true): the position cannot be known, so re-read before downloading. Exit 4 only when the whole thread was read and holds none; a read that lost a page (`messagesIncomplete: true`) is exit 0 with what it found.

notes.path: the file, downloaded in-process from the presigned URL and saved under ~/.aula/attachments unless --out names a path. Read a PDF with `pdftotext -layout`. A link (kind link) has no bytes and is refused as a usage error.

as `attachment`, for a post's attachment: `post-attachment <postId> [index]`, the index `posts` shows. An unknown post id, or an index the post does not have, is a usage error naming what it does have.

notes.envelope: `truncated: true` means more rows matched than are here — raise --limit, or narrow with --since where the command takes it. `limit` is null when nothing capped the read (`--since` alone, or a command with no default cap). `fetchedAt` is when the oldest response in the answer was read from Aula; responses are cached ten minutes, and --no-cache makes it now.
notes.files: Fælles Filer, newest first: timetables (skema), holiday plans, policies. No URL: `commonfile <id|text from the title>` downloads one. `status` other than available is a file the virus scan has not passed, which cannot be fetched yet.

notes.path: as `attachment`, for a shared file. An ambiguous title is refused with the candidates rather than guessed at — the shelf holds near-identical names across years.

notes.supported: which vendor widgets the family's institutions expose, and whether this tool has an integration for each (`supported`). `capability` is what the integration answers: weekly-plan, weekly-letter, tasks, assignments or reminders.

on_exit_4._note: one plan per vendor, each with `items: []` and status ok or skipped; [] when no vendor serves the capability

notes.plans: one plan per vendor that serves the capability, for --week (this ISO week by default; --next for next). The same shape for weekly-letter, tasks, assignments, reminders and homework (which reads the three homework capabilities at once). Exit 1 with no body when nothing readable came back and a vendor failed; the vendor's reason is on stderr, and a failed read is never cached. `status` is what tells a failed vendor read from a quiet week — both are `items: []`. ok: the vendor answered for every child asked. partial: items are real and `warnings` names who is missing. failed: nothing readable came back and `warnings` says why — never an empty week. skipped: the vendor was not asked, because no selected child attends a school. `provider: "unavailable"` is a capability that threw before any vendor answered. `items[]` keys are whatever the vendor gave: every one is optional, and `date` may be an ISO date or the vendor's own Danish label.

notes.ids: the four id spaces Aula uses, resolved once: a child's `id` is the institution-profile id nearly every endpoint wants, `profileId` the person, `userId` the token the vendor widgets key on. `isSteppedUp: false` means sensitive threads may be masked or missing — `refresh-stepup` restores it while the broker session lives. `mitidUsername` is what Meebook, Systematic and SkolePortal key their session on; null means those vendors fall back to the guardian id and say so in `warnings`.

notes.session: answered from disk, with no request and no token refresh, so it can run beside anything. `session` is Aula's last verdict on the stored login — state accepted or rejected, when, and whether the session was stepped up (null when not yet observed) — or null when no command has reached Aula with it. An expired access token is renewed silently by the next read and is never a reason to log in; a rejected state, or exit 5 from a read, is — and a login is the user's to agree to. Aula publishes no lifetime for the refresh token or for step-up, so `checkedAt` is the honest substitute.

notes.checks: every endpoint called for real, never from cache. `status` is ok, warn, skip or fail; warn is a call that worked but answered something API.md names as a known symptom (an empty feed from a wrong id set, a session that is not stepped up), and `note` says what it will do to your output. The report is on stdout on exit 1 as well — the one exit 1 in this tool with a body — and the error line still closes stderr.
